sections.html:
Baxter County is in the Ozarks of north-central Arkansas, just south of the Missouri line. Bull Shoals Lake and Norfork Lake give the area its Twin Lakes nickname, and lake property is a big part of the housing market. Mountain Home is the county seat and largest city, with 12,825 residents in 2020. Other incorporated places are Cotter, Gassville, Briarcliff, Norfork, Salesville, Lakeview and Big Flat. Mountain Home, Cotter and Norfork run the three public school districts.

The 2020 count was 41,627 people and 22,699 housing units, with 74.5 percent of occupied units owner-occupied. The median age is 52.7 and 31.5 percent of residents are 65 or older, which matters because owners 65 or older, or disabled, can qualify for a freeze on taxable value.

Real estate is by far the biggest piece of the local base, so a shift in house values changes the whole county's tax picture.

Work is divided among three offices: the assessor sets values, the County Clerk's office handles requests to the equalization board, and the collector sends bills and takes payment. The collector's office is at #8 East 7th Street, Mountain Home, AR 72653, phone 870-425-8300, with live support Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. The courthouse is at 1 East 7th Street.

Collected revenue goes to the county treasurer at least monthly. Since 2016 receipts are no longer printed automatically, so enclose an email address or a stamped return envelope with a mailed payment. E-statements and e-receipts are available by sign-up.

Baxter County is one of five north-central counties reappraising in 2026, along with Marion, Izard, Stone and Boone. A 2023 state law requires counties to appraise real estate at current market value at least every four years. The last round raised values 35 percent across residential, commercial and new construction in 2022. That is market value, not what owners paid, and caps and freezes keep taxes from rising at the same rate.

  • Recent buyers may receive a sales validation form to complete.
  • In a reappraisal year, notices go out in July to owners whose values increase.
  • Appeals are scheduled with the equalization board in August and heard in September.
  • The homestead credit was $500 in 2024 and $600 for 2025, and owners over 65 or fully disabled may qualify for a freeze on top of it. Call the assessor for the current credit amount.

Section 26-27-317 lets an owner apply to the equalization board up to the third Monday in August. After the hearing the board owes you written notice of its decision, at least ten business days later, spelling out your right to appeal to county court.

The collector takes payments starting the first business day of March and stops counting a bill as timely on October 15. After that date, real or personal property tax is delinquent and a 10 percent penalty is added.

  • Installment payments are accepted between the first business day of March and October 15.
  • By December 1 the collector passes the delinquent list to a legal newspaper, and publication must follow within seven days.
  • Online payment runs through links to arkansastaxsearch.com.
  • Personal property such as vehicles and boats must be assessed by May 31 each year.

Bills here come in arrears: the one arriving in March reflects the prior assessment year. Anyone closing in spring should ask the title company how the current year's unbilled tax is being prorated.

Years of unpaid real estate tax can send the land to the Commissioner of State Lands, which sets up a sale. Section 26-37-301 requires the Commissioner to notify the owner and anyone with a recorded interest, and to allow redemption once all taxes, penalties, interest and costs are paid.

A sale cannot be held until a year after certification. When the property is a homestead and nothing proves the owner got the certified letter, personal service must be arranged at least 60 days ahead of the sale. Someone with no ownership interest may redeem too, by paying what is due.

You can sell with tax owed, as long as the whole amount, penalty included, is cleared. Phone the collector at 870-425-8300 for the payoff before choosing a closing date. The title company takes that figure and sends the county its money out of your proceeds.

Bring the deed or a recent statement and photo ID. Heirs living in other states can usually sign before a notary and send the papers back.

Older owners and lake property raise the same situations repeatedly:

  • Inherited houses where heirs live in other states and the property sits empty.
  • Homes with deferred maintenance, since a lender-financed buyer may require repairs.
  • Owners whose reappraisal notice raised the value and who want to sell before the new bill arrives.
  • Tax or insurance bills that have piled up during a long illness or move to care.

A cash sale skips the lender's repair requirements and the appraisal wait. You describe the house, receive an offer, choose a closing date and the title company clears the tax from proceeds.

If your value is likely to rise, buyers may notice before you do. A new notice shows up in July, and a buyer who sees a higher assessed value may expect a higher bill. Caps and freezes soften the effect, but they do not apply to every owner, and a new owner has to apply for his or her own benefits.

Many sellers decide to list before the new bill lands. Others wait until after appeals are decided so they can point to a settled number. Either choice is fine. What matters is that you know which tax year the title company is prorating, and that the contract says who pays the current year.

Keep the deed, your newest tax statement, any equalization board notice, receipts for repairs and the names on the title in one folder. For lake property, add dock or shoreline permits and septic records. For a house you inherited, add the death certificate and court papers. A complete folder lets the title company move quickly and prevents the most common closing delays.

No interstate crosses the county. US 62 and US 412 run together east to west, and Arkansas 5 is the only route running north to south throughout. The nearest commercial airport is Springfield-Branson in Missouri, though the county has its own Baxter County Airport. Mention these when describing a house to out-of-state buyers.

faqs.q: When is the Baxter County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: October 15. The collector accepts payment from the first business day of March through that date, and unpaid tax is delinquent afterward with a 10 percent penalty.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Baxter County value?
faqs.a: Request a hearing with the county equalization board through the County Clerk's office. State law sets the application deadline at the third Monday in August.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead credit in Baxter County?
faqs.a: It was $500 in 2024 and $600 for 2025. Ask the assessor's office for the current amount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Baxter County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The amount due, including the 10 percent penalty after October 15, has to be settled. Ask the collector at 870-425-8300 for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Which Baxter County towns have their own school district?
faqs.a: Mountain Home, Cotter and Norfork each have a public school district.
